title: Okta Domain 6 questions (6.1, 6.2)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with Okta.

questions.topic: System Log Search and Filter Expressions
questions.stem: An admin wants every failed event for the user ana@example.com in the System Log. Which filter expression is correct?
questions.answer: actor.alternateId eq "ana@example.com" and outcome.result eq "FAILURE"
questions.explanation: System Log filters use field paths such as actor.alternateId and outcome.result with operators like eq joined by and. The other choices use made-up fields, programming operators, or or, which would also return every other user's failures.

questions.topic: System Log Search and Filter Expressions
questions.stem: Which System Log filter expression returns sign-ins that start an Okta session?
questions.answer: eventType eq "user.session.start"
questions.explanation: user.session.start records the creation of an Okta session at sign-in. user.session.end records a session ending.

questions.topic: System Log Search and Filter Expressions
questions.stem: An admin wants all lifecycle events, such as user creation, activation and deactivation, in one search. Which filter expression BEST does this?
questions.answer: eventType sw "user.lifecycle"
questions.explanation: The sw operator matches values that start with the given text, so it catches every user.lifecycle event. eq needs an exact match and no event type is just user.lifecycle.

questions.topic: System Log Search and Filter Expressions
questions.stem: Where in the Admin Console does an admin open the System Log?
questions.answer: Reports > System Log
questions.explanation: The System Log is under the Reports menu. Individual user and app pages also link to their own events.

questions.topic: System Log Search and Filter Expressions
questions.stem: The security team gives an admin a suspicious IP address and asks for every event from it. Which filter expression should the admin use?
questions.answer: client.ipAddress eq "203.0.113.10"
questions.explanation: The requester's IP address is recorded under the client object of each event. The actor, target and outcome objects do not hold the IP address.

questions.topic: System Log Search and Filter Expressions
questions.stem: A help desk lead looking at a user's profile wants to jump straight to that user's System Log events. What is the quickest way?
choices: Run the Okta Usage report for the user
Use the View Logs link on the user's profile
Open the user in the Profile Editor
Export the list from Directory > People
questions.answer: Use the View Logs link on the user's profile
questions.explanation: The profile's View Logs link opens the System Log already filtered to that user. The Okta Usage report summarizes sign-ins but not every event.

questions.stem: A user says she was locked out yesterday afternoon. Which event type shows exactly when the lockout happened?
questions.answer: user.account.lock
questions.explanation: user.account.lock is written when an account becomes Locked out. Suspension is an admin action recorded as a lifecycle event.

questions.stem: Management asks who deactivated a former employee's account last week. Which event type should the admin search, reading the actor field of the result?
questions.answer: user.lifecycle.deactivate
questions.explanation: Deactivation is recorded as user.lifecycle.deactivate, and its actor is the admin or process that performed it. Removing an app assignment is a different event.

questions.stem: An admin needs to know when a user joined the Finance group and whether a group rule or a person added him. Which event type should the admin search?
questions.answer: group.user_membership.add
questions.explanation: group.user_membership.add records a user being added to a group, and its actor shows who or what added the user. application.user_membership.add is for app assignments.

questions.stem: Which event type shows that a user was assigned to an app integration?
questions.answer: application.user_membership.add
questions.explanation: Assigning an app to a user writes application.user_membership.add. user.authentication.sso records the user actually signing in to the app.

questions.stem: A user is denied by an app's authentication policy, and the admin wants the event that shows the policy decision and the rule involved. Which event type should the admin search?
questions.answer: policy.evaluate_sign_on
questions.explanation: policy.evaluate_sign_on records the policy evaluation, including the outcome and the matched policy and rule. user.session.start only shows the Okta session being created.

questions.stem: An auditor asks who gave a user an administrator role. Which event type should the admin search?
questions.answer: user.account.privilege.grant
questions.explanation: Granting an admin role to a user writes user.account.privilege.grant. A group membership event only matters if the role was assigned to a group.

questions.stem: An admin wants to confirm that a user actually signed in to the payroll app through Okta single sign-on yesterday. Which event type should the admin look for?
questions.answer: user.authentication.sso
questions.explanation: user.authentication.sso records SSO into an app. user.session.start only proves the user signed in to Okta, not to the app.

questions.stem: In a System Log event, which object identifies who or what performed the action?
questions.answer: actor
questions.explanation: The actor is the user, admin or system process that performed the action. The target is the object the action affected.

questions.stem: An admin opens a user.lifecycle.deactivate event and wants to know which account was deactivated. Which part of the event should the admin read?
questions.answer: target
questions.explanation: The target lists the objects the action was performed on, here the deactivated user. The actor is the admin who did it.

questions.stem: A sign-in event shows a FAILURE result. Which field explains why it failed?
questions.answer: outcome.reason
questions.explanation: outcome.result only says success or failure, while outcome.reason gives the cause, such as invalid credentials. The user agent describes the browser.

questions.stem: An admin wants to see which browser, operating system and country a suspicious sign-in came from. Where in the event is this recorded?
choices: In the target details listed in the event
In the actor details of the event
In the event's display message only
In the client details of the event
questions.answer: In the client details of the event
questions.explanation: The client object holds the IP address, geographic location and user agent of the request. The actor identifies the user, not the device.

questions.stem: An admin sees several events from one sign-in attempt and wants to group the events that belong to the same request. Which value helps with this?
questions.answer: The transaction ID
questions.explanation: Events from one request share a transaction ID, so it links them together. Many unrelated events share the same actor name or severity.

questions.stem: A policy.evaluate_sign_on event has the outcome result DENY. What does this tell the admin?
choices: A policy rule blocked the request
The user's password was typed incorrectly
The System Log could not record the event
The user's account was deactivated by an admin
questions.answer: A policy rule blocked the request
questions.explanation: For policy evaluation events, DENY means the matched rule did not allow access. A wrong password produces a failed authentication event instead.

questions.stem: An admin wants to see which risk behaviors Okta detected for a sign-in, such as a new device or new location. Where in the event should the admin look?
choices: In the target list of the event's details
In the debug data under debugContext
In the legacy event type field of the event
questions.answer: In the debug data under debugContext
questions.explanation: Okta puts extra details such as detected behaviors and risk information in debugContext.debugData. The target lists affected objects, not risk signals.

questions.stem: An admin needs a list of who signed in to Okta during last quarter. Which built-in report BEST fits?
questions.answer: Okta Usage report
questions.explanation: The Okta Usage report shows which users signed in to Okta during a period. Application Usage covers sign-ins to individual apps.

questions.stem: Before renewing a license, an app owner wants to know the last time each user signed in to that app. Which report should the admin run?
questions.answer: Application Usage report
questions.explanation: The Application Usage report lists users and their sign-ins to a selected app integration. The Okta Usage report is about Okta sign-ins, not a single app.

questions.stem: Security wants a list of which authenticators each user has enrolled. Which report provides this?
questions.answer: MFA Usage report
questions.explanation: The MFA Usage report lists enrolled authenticators per user. The Telephony Usage report covers SMS and voice delivery.

questions.stem: A compliance officer asks for the current status of Okta passwords across the org, as a downloadable file. Which report should the admin provide?
questions.answer: Okta Password Health report
questions.explanation: The Okta Password Health report is a downloadable file describing the state of users' Okta passwords. The MFA Usage report covers authenticators, not passwords.

questions.stem: An admin wants to find apps that support provisioning but do not have it turned on yet. Which report helps?
questions.answer: Provisioning Capable Apps report
questions.explanation: The Provisioning Capable Apps report highlights integrations that could provision but do not. The SAML Capable Apps report is about SSO options.

questions.stem: An auditor wants to know which users and groups hold administrator roles and with which resource sets. Which report should the admin run?
questions.answer: Admin Role Assignments report
questions.explanation: The Admin Role Assignments report lists role assignments, including roles and resource sets. Usage reports cover sign-in activity.

questions.stem: An investigator needs each individual event for a user, with the actor, IP address and outcome of every action. Which source should the admin use?
questions.answer: The System Log
questions.explanation: Reports give ready-made summaries, while the System Log holds the individual event records with actor, client and outcome details. Usage reports leave out most event detail.

questions.stem: An admin wants a downloadable report of risky events, such as failed logins and locked-out users, over the last month. Which report should the admin run?
questions.answer: Suspicious Activity report
questions.explanation: The Suspicious Activity report queries the System Log for suspicious events such as failed logins and lockouts and can be downloaded as CSV. The Telephony Usage report covers SMS and voice delivery, and Deprovision Details covers deprovisioning.

questions.stem: An auditor asks for System Log events from five months ago, but the admin finds nothing older than about three months. What explains this?
choices: The System Log deletes events after each release
Only Super Administrators can see older events
Events older than 30 days must be restored by an admin
Okta keeps System Log events for 90 days
questions.answer: Okta keeps System Log events for 90 days
questions.explanation: The System Log keeps events for 90 days, so older events must come from an export or a SIEM. The admin role does not change retention.

questions.stem: Compliance requires sign-in events to be kept for 2 years. What should the admin set up?
choices: A longer maximum session lifetime in the global session policy
Log streaming or System Log API collection into a SIEM
A scheduled Okta Usage report sent by email
A larger log retention value set in the org's password policy
questions.answer: Log streaming or System Log API collection into a SIEM
questions.explanation: Events must leave Okta before the 90-day limit, through log streaming or the System Log API, to be kept longer. Reports do not hold every event.

questions.stem: Which standard administrator role can set up log streaming to an external destination?
questions.answer: Super Administrator
questions.explanation: Okta's role comparison lists log streaming management for Super Administrators only. Report and Read-only Administrators can view events but not configure streaming.

questions.stem: A help desk admin with only the Help Desk Administrator role cannot open the System Log. What is the reason?
choices: The Help Desk Administrator role does not include System Log access
The System Log is turned off for help desk orgs
The help desk admin must enroll Okta Verify first
The System Log only opens from a Preview org
questions.answer: The Help Desk Administrator role does not include System Log access
questions.explanation: Help Desk Administrators manage user passwords, unlocks and authenticators but do not get System Log access. Adding a role such as Report Administrator would grant it.

questions.stem: An admin wants the current System Log search results in a spreadsheet for a meeting. What is the simplest way?
choices: Copy the events from the Okta status page
Run the Okta Password Health report
Open a support case and request a copy
Download the search results as a CSV file
questions.answer: Download the search results as a CSV file
questions.explanation: The System Log can export the current results as CSV. Support cases are not needed for data the admin can download.

questions.stem: A developer wants a script to pull System Log events into an internal tool every hour. What should the script call?
questions.answer: The System Log API
questions.explanation: The System Log API returns log events with the same filters as the console. The Users and Groups APIs manage directory objects, not events.

questions.stem: An external auditor needs to view and download reports and the System Log but must not change anything in the org. Which standard role fits BEST?
questions.answer: Report Administrator
questions.explanation: Report Administrators can view and download reports and the System Log with no change rights. Application Administrators can change apps.

questions.topic: System Log Search and Filter Expressions
questions.stem: An admin must find when a user was locked out and why. Put the steps in order.
items: Set the date range to cover the reported time
Enter a filter such as eventType eq "user.account.lock"
Open the matching event and expand its details
Read the actor, client and outcome fields
questions.explanation: The admin opens the log, narrows the time window, filters on the event type, and then reads the event's details for the cause and source.

questions.stem: An admin wants to give two auditors access to the System Log without the right to change users. Which TWO standard roles include System Log access?
questions.explanation: Okta's role comparison grants System Log viewing to Report and Read-only Administrators, among others. Help Desk, Group and Group Membership Administrators do not get it.

questions.stem: Match each event type to what it records.

pairs.match: A user started an Okta session
A user was assigned to an app

questions.explanation: Event types name the object and the action, which makes them easy to filter on. Support cases are handled outside the org and do not appear as System Log events.

questions.stem: Within minutes, users across the whole company report that Okta sign-in is failing or very slow. What should the admin check FIRST?
choices: The System Log for each user, one at a time
The Okta Community forum for similar posts
status.okta.com for an incident affecting the org's cell
questions.answer: status.okta.com for an incident affecting the org's cell
questions.explanation: A sudden org-wide problem may be an Okta service incident, which is published on status.okta.com. Checking users one by one wastes time during a possible outage.

questions.stem: An admin wants to be told automatically when Okta posts an incident or maintenance notice. What should the admin do?
choices: Create a group rule that adds the admin team to a group
Subscribe to notifications on the Okta status page
Turn on an Early Access feature that sends incident alerts
Add the admins to the Everyone group
questions.answer: Subscribe to notifications on the Okta status page
questions.explanation: The status page offers subscriptions for incident and maintenance updates. Group rules and features in the org do not send service status alerts.

questions.stem: status.okta.com shows a degraded-performance incident for the cell that hosts the org, matching what users report. What is the BEST next step?
choices: Reset the passwords of every user in the org
Rotate the signing certificates of every SAML app now
Follow the incident updates and tell users it is a known issue
Turn off the global session policy until it ends
questions.answer: Follow the incident updates and tell users it is a known issue
questions.explanation: During a published incident the right step is to communicate and follow Okta's updates. Changing credentials or policies would add risk without fixing the service.

questions.stem: The status page shows every service as operational, but one user cannot sign in. What should the admin do next?
choices: Review that user's events in the System Log
Wait for Okta to post an incident on the status page
Open a support case at the highest severity level
Reset the authenticators of every user
questions.answer: Review that user's events in the System Log
questions.explanation: When the service is healthy, a single-user issue is usually an account or policy problem that the System Log explains. It does not justify a top-severity case.

questions.stem: An admin needs to know whether Okta plans maintenance that could affect sign-in this weekend. Where should the admin look?
choices: The System Log events filtered for maintenance activity
The scheduled maintenance listed on status.okta.com
The Okta Usage report for last week
The release notes for the Preview org
questions.answer: The scheduled maintenance listed on status.okta.com
questions.explanation: The status page lists scheduled maintenance as well as live incidents. The System Log only records what has already happened in the org.

questions.stem: Users reach the Okta dashboard normally, but a third-party SaaS app fails for everyone with an error from the app itself. The Okta status page shows no incident. What is the BEST next step?
choices: Open an Okta case at the highest severity
Clear the sessions of every user in the org
Check the app vendor's own status page and contact the vendor
Deactivate and reactivate every user assigned to the app
questions.answer: Check the app vendor's own status page and contact the vendor
questions.explanation: Okta is healthy and the error comes from the app, so the vendor's status and support are the right place. Clearing sessions does not repair an app outage.

questions.stem: During the Okta Certified Professional Performance exam, which resource does the study guide allow a candidate to use for looking up how to configure an Okta feature?
choices: The Okta Help Center and its product documentation
The Okta status page at status.okta.com
The System Log of the exam org
questions.answer: The Okta Help Center and its product documentation
questions.explanation: The Performance exam study guide allows access to the Okta Help Center, which links to the admin product documentation. The status page reports service health, not configuration steps.

questions.stem: Okta documentation pages can be viewed for Identity Engine or Classic Engine. How can an admin tell which engine the org uses?
choices: Look up the org's entry on status.okta.com for the engine type
Run the Okta Usage report for the org
Search the System Log for an engine event
Check the version shown in the Admin Console footer
questions.answer: Check the version shown in the Admin Console footer
questions.explanation: The Admin Console footer shows the version with E for Identity Engine or C for Classic Engine. The status page shows service health, not the engine.

questions.stem: A developer needs reference details for Okta's management APIs and SDKs. Which site BEST fits?
questions.answer: developer.okta.com
questions.explanation: developer.okta.com hosts the API reference, SDK guides and developer tutorials. The status page and release notes do not document API calls.

questions.stem: An admin follows a documentation page, but the menu names and steps do not match the Admin Console of an Identity Engine org. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: The org has moved to a different Okta cell since then
The admin is reading the Classic Engine version of the page
The admin lacks the Report Administrator role
The page only applies to Preview orgs
questions.answer: The admin is reading the Classic Engine version of the page
questions.explanation: Okta publishes separate Identity Engine and Classic Engine versions of many pages, and terms differ between them. The cell does not change the console menus.

questions.stem: An admin is setting up SAML for an app from the Okta Integration Network and needs the vendor-specific values to enter on the app's side. Where is the BEST place to find them?
choices: The Okta status page for the org's cell
The setup instructions linked from the app's Sign On tab
The System Log filtered to the app
questions.answer: The setup instructions linked from the app's Sign On tab
questions.explanation: OIN SAML integrations link to setup instructions that explain what to configure in the app. The System Log shows events, not configuration values.

questions.stem: A new admin wants to compare exactly which permissions each standard administrator role includes before assigning one. Where should the admin look?
choices: The Okta status page incident history
The Application Usage report for the org
The release notes for the next Preview release of the Admin Console
The standard roles and permissions page in the Okta documentation
questions.answer: The standard roles and permissions page in the Okta documentation
questions.explanation: Okta's documentation has a comparison of standard roles and their permissions. The Admin Role Assignments report shows who holds roles, but the documentation explains what each role can do.

questions.topic: Release Notes and Early Access Features
questions.stem: The release notes describe a self-service Early Access feature that an admin cannot find in the org. Where should the admin turn it on?
choices: Security > Authenticators in the Admin Console
The Okta status page subscription settings
Settings > Features in the Admin Console
Reports > System Log in the Admin Console
questions.answer: Settings > Features in the Admin Console
questions.explanation: Self-service Early Access features are enabled by an admin on the Features page under Settings. Authenticator settings do not list new product features.

questions.topic: Release Notes and Early Access Features
questions.stem: What is the main purpose of an Okta Preview org compared with a Production org?
choices: It keeps System Log events for much longer than a Production org does
It allows unlimited users without a contract
It is the only type of Okta org that can host SAML single sign-on apps
It receives each release earlier so admins can test changes first
questions.answer: It receives each release earlier so admins can test changes first
questions.explanation: Preview orgs get releases before Production orgs, giving admins time to test. Log retention and app support are not what makes a Preview org different.

questions.topic: Release Notes and Early Access Features
questions.stem: Where should an admin read about the features and fixes included in Okta's latest release?
choices: The release notes in the Okta documentation
The System Log for the release weekend
The Okta Usage report for the month
questions.answer: The release notes in the Okta documentation
questions.explanation: Okta publishes release notes for each release in its documentation. The System Log records org activity, not product changes.

questions.topic: Release Notes and Early Access Features
questions.stem: Which statement BEST describes an Early Access feature?
choices: A feature that Okta turns on for every org automatically at release
An optional feature admins can turn on before general availability
A feature that only Okta Support staff can see
A feature that has been retired from the product
questions.answer: An optional feature admins can turn on before general availability
questions.explanation: Early Access features are opt-in and come before general availability. Features that are on for everyone are generally available.

questions.topic: Release Notes and Early Access Features
questions.stem: After a weekend, the admin notices that a page in the Admin Console looks different, and no one in the company changed any settings. What is the BEST way to find out whether an Okta release explains it?
choices: Check status.okta.com for an active incident
Search the System Log for admin changes
Post the question on the Okta Community forum and wait for replies
Read the release notes for the most recent release
questions.answer: Read the release notes for the most recent release
questions.explanation: Release notes list interface changes that came with a release. The System Log would show admin changes, which the scenario already rules out.

questions.topic: Release Notes and Early Access Features
questions.stem: A release note says a new feature is available, but it appears in the company's Preview org and not yet in its Production org. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: The Production org needs a separate support case for every new feature
Production orgs never receive Early Access features from a release
Releases reach Preview orgs before they reach Production orgs
The Production org is hosted on a slower Okta cell
questions.answer: Releases reach Preview orgs before they reach Production orgs
questions.explanation: Okta rolls each release to Preview orgs first and to Production orgs later. Production orgs can use Early Access features once they arrive.

questions.topic: Okta Community, Knowledge Base and Learning
questions.stem: An admin wants advice from other Okta customers on how they structure groups for many subsidiaries. Which resource BEST fits?
choices: The System Log of the org
questions.answer: The Okta Community forum
questions.explanation: The Community forum is where customers and Okta staff discuss design questions. A support case is for problems with the org, not peer advice.

questions.topic: Okta Community, Knowledge Base and Learning
questions.stem: An admin wants Okta to add a feature that does not exist yet. What is the BEST way to request it?
choices: Submit or vote for an idea in the Okta Community
Post the request on the status page
Turn on every Early Access feature
questions.answer: Submit or vote for an idea in the Okta Community
questions.explanation: Okta collects feature requests as ideas in its Community, where others can vote on them. Support cases are for help with the current product.

questions.topic: Okta Community, Knowledge Base and Learning
questions.stem: Users see a specific error message during SSO, and the admin suspects it is a known issue. What is the quickest resource to check before opening a case?
choices: The incident history on the Okta status page for the org's cell
The knowledge base articles in the Okta Help Center
The Okta Usage report for the org
questions.answer: The knowledge base articles in the Okta Help Center
questions.explanation: Knowledge base articles explain known errors and their fixes. The status page covers service incidents, not specific configuration errors.

questions.topic: Okta Community, Knowledge Base and Learning
questions.stem: A new Okta admin wants structured courses and practice environments to build skills. Which resource BEST fits?
questions.answer: Okta Learning
questions.explanation: Okta Learning offers courses and learning paths for admins. The API reference documents calls but does not teach administration.

questions.topic: Okta Community, Knowledge Base and Learning
questions.stem: A candidate wants the official study guide and registration details for the Okta Certified Professional exam. Where should the candidate look?
choices: The System Log of the org
questions.answer: The Okta Certification site
questions.explanation: The Okta Certification site publishes exam study guides and registration information. The Features page only lists product features.

questions.topic: Okta Community, Knowledge Base and Learning
questions.stem: A developer has a question about calling an Okta API from custom code and wants help from other developers. Which resource BEST fits?
questions.answer: The Okta Developer Forum
questions.explanation: The Developer Forum is the community space for API and SDK questions. Reports describe the org, not how to write code against Okta.

questions.stem: An admin has a problem that the documentation and knowledge base do not solve. Where should the admin open a support case?
choices: On the Okta status page incident form
In the Okta Community ideas board
In the Okta Help Center under Get Support
In the Admin Console System Log
questions.answer: In the Okta Help Center under Get Support
questions.explanation: Support cases are opened through the Okta Help Center's support section. The Community ideas board is for feature requests.

questions.stem: Okta Support asks an admin which org a new case is about. Which detail identifies the org MOST precisely?
choices: The org's Okta URL, such as example.okta.com
The name of the company's HR system
The expiry date of an app's SAML certificate
questions.answer: The org's Okta URL, such as example.okta.com
questions.explanation: Each Okta org has its own URL, which lets Support locate the exact org and its cell. An email address, HR system or certificate date does not identify the org.

questions.stem: Okta Support is investigating a browser-based SSO failure and asks for a capture of the network traffic during the failing attempt. What should the admin provide?
choices: A HAR file recorded while the failure happens
A copy of the global session policy
questions.answer: A HAR file recorded while the failure happens
questions.explanation: A HAR file records the browser's requests and responses, showing where the SSO flow breaks. Reports do not capture what the browser exchanged.

questions.stem: Okta Support asks for permission to sign in to the org to look at a configuration problem. Where does an admin grant this?
choices: Security > Administrators, by adding Okta Support as an admin user
Directory > People, by creating a new user account for Okta Support
Reports > System Log, by sharing the current filter
Settings > Account, in the Give Access to Okta Support section
questions.answer: Settings > Account, in the Give Access to Okta Support section
questions.explanation: Okta Support access is granted from the Account settings page, without creating accounts for Support staff. Creating a user for Support would add an unmanaged account.

questions.stem: What does selecting Grant impersonation for a case give Okta Support?
choices: Super Administrator access until the case closes
Access to the org's user passwords for one week
Read-only admin access to the org for 24 hours
Permanent read-only access to the System Log
questions.answer: Read-only admin access to the org for 24 hours
questions.explanation: Impersonation for a case gives Support read-only admin access for 24 hours. It never grants super admin rights or password access.

questions.stem: Which of these issues justifies the highest severity when opening an Okta support case?
choices: A question about a feature in a Preview org
A request for a link to a documentation page
A spelling error on the custom sign-in page
No users can sign in to the production org
questions.answer: No users can sign in to the production org
questions.explanation: The highest severity is for a production outage with major business impact. Questions and cosmetic issues use lower severities.

questions.stem: When Okta Support opens a case itself and assigns it to an engineer, which setting lets that engineer access the org's settings?
choices: Approving support access for self-assigned cases in the account settings
Adding the engineer to the Everyone group in the org
Turning on an Early Access feature for Okta Support
Sharing a saved System Log search with the engineer
questions.answer: Approving support access for self-assigned cases in the account settings
questions.explanation: The Give Access to Okta Support section has a separate approval for cases that Support opens and assigns to itself. Adding Support staff to groups is not how access is given.

questions.stem: The Okta status page lists the health of many separate cells. Which cell's status matters when the admin's users report problems?
choices: The cell nearest to each user's location
The cell that hosts the company's org
Every cell, because all orgs share them
The cell listed first on the status page
questions.answer: The cell that hosts the company's org
questions.explanation: Each Okta org runs on one cell, so only that cell's status explains the org's problems. Users' locations do not change which cell serves the org.

questions.stem: Users report sign-in problems after a change. Put the support steps in the order an admin should follow.
items: Search the knowledge base for the error
Gather affected users, times and System Log events
Open a support case with a fitting severity
Grant Okta Support access if they ask for it
questions.explanation: Ruling out an Okta incident and known issues first saves time; a case with good evidence is solved faster, and access is granted only when Support requests it.

questions.stem: An admin is opening a case about users failing to sign in. Which TWO items are MOST useful to include?
choices: Timestamps with time zone and the affected usernames
A screenshot of the Okta marketing website
A list of every app in the org
answers: Timestamps with time zone and the affected usernames
questions.explanation: Who, when and the matching events let Support trace the failure. Passwords must never be shared, and unrelated screenshots or app lists add noise.

questions.topic: Okta Community, Knowledge Base and Learning
questions.stem: Match each need to the Okta resource that BEST fits it.

pairs.item: Find out whether Okta has a live incident
Ask other customers for design advice

questions.explanation: Each resource has a clear role: service health, product docs, developer docs, peer discussion and training. The end-user dashboard only launches apps.
